```
A) <option label> (recommended)
  ✅ <pro — concrete, observable, ≥40 chars>
  ❌ <con — honest, ≥40 chars>
B) <option label>
  ✅ <pro>
  ❌ <con>
Net: <one-line synthesis of what you're actually trading off>
```

D-numbering: first question in a skill invocation is `D1`; increment yourself. This is a model-level instruction, not a runtime counter.

ELI10 is always present, in plain English, not function names. Recommendation is ALWAYS present. Keep the `(recommended)` label; AUTO_DECIDE depends on it.

Completeness: use `Completeness: N/10` only when options differ in coverage. 10 = complete, 7 = happy path, 3 = shortcut. If options differ in kind, write: `Note: options differ in kind, not coverage — no completeness score.`

Pros / cons: use ✅ and ❌. Minimum 2 pros and 1 con per option when the choice is real; Minimum 40 characters per bullet. Hard-stop escape for one-way/destructive confirmations: `✅ No cons — this is a hard-stop choice`.

Neutral posture: `Recommendation: <default> — this is a taste call, no strong preference either way`; `(recommended)` STAYS on the default option for AUTO_DECIDE.

Effort both-scales: when an option involves effort, label both human-team and CC+gstack time, e.g. `(human: ~2 days / CC: ~15 min)`. Makes AI compression visible at decision time.

Net line closes the tradeoff. Per-skill instructions may add stricter rules.

### Handling 5+ options — split, never drop

AskUserQuestion caps every call at **4 options**. With 5+ real options, NEVER
drop, merge, or silently defer one to fit. Pick a compliant shape:

- **Batch into ≤4-groups** — for coherent alternatives (e.g. version bumps,
  layout variants). One call, 5th surfaced only if first 4 don't fit.
- **Split per-option** — for independent scope items (e.g. "ship E1..E6?").
  Fire N sequential calls, one per option. Default to this when unsure.

Per-option call shape: `D<N>.k` header (e.g. D3.1..D3.5), ELI10 per option,
Recommendation, kind-note (no completeness score — Include/Defer/Cut/Hold are
decision actions), and 4 buckets:
**A) Include**, **B) Defer**, **C) Cut**, **D) Hold** (stop chain, discuss).

After the chain, fire `D<N>.final` to validate the assembled set (reprompt
dependency conflicts) and confirm shipping it. Use `D<N>.revise-<k>` to
revise one option without re-running the chain.

For N>6, fire a `D<N>.0` meta-AskUserQuestion first (proceed / narrow / batch).

question_ids for split chains: `<skill>-split-<option-slug>` (kebab-case ASCII,
≤64 chars, `-2`/`-3` suffix on collision). The runtime checker
(`bin/gstack-question-preference`) refuses `never-ask` on any `*-split-*` id,
so split chains are never AUTO_DECIDE-eligible — the user's option set is sacred.

**Full rule + worked examples + Hold/dependency semantics:** see
`docs/askuserquestion-split.md` in the gstack repo. Read on demand when N>4.

**Non-ASCII characters — write directly, never \u-escape.** When any string
field contains Chinese (繁體/簡體), Japanese, Korean, or other non-ASCII text,
emit the literal UTF-8 characters; never escape them as `\uXXXX` (the pipe is
UTF-8 native, and manual escaping miscodes long CJK strings). Only `\n`,
`\t`, `\"`, `\\` remain allowed. Full rationale + worked example: see
`docs/askuserquestion-cjk.md`. Read on demand when a question contains CJK.

### Self-check before emitting

Before calling AskUserQuestion, verify:
- [ ] D<N> header present
- [ ] ELI10 paragraph present (stakes line too)
- [ ] Recommendation line present with concrete reason
- [ ] Completeness scored (coverage) OR kind-note present (kind)
- [ ] Every option has ≥2 ✅ and ≥1 ❌, each ≥40 chars (or hard-stop escape)
- [ ] (recommended) label on one option (even for neutral-posture)
- [ ] Dual-scale effort labels on effort-bearing options (human / CC)
- [ ] Net line closes the decision
- [ ] You are calling the tool, not writing prose — unless `CONDUCTOR_SESSION: true` (then prose is the DEFAULT, not the tool) OR the documented failure fallback applies (then: prose with the mandatory triad — issue ELI10, per-choice Completeness, Recommendation + `(recommended)` — and a "reply with a letter" instruction, then STOP)
- [ ] Non-ASCII characters (CJK / accents) written directly, NOT \u-escaped
- [ ] If you had 5+ options, you split (or batched into ≤4-groups) — did NOT drop any
- [ ] If you split, you checked dependencies between options before firing the chain
- [ ] If a per-option Hold fires, you stopped the chain immediately (didn't queue)

```bash
      echo "symbol-aware code lookup. See \"## GBrain Search Guidance\" in CLAUDE.md."

_BRAIN_SYNC_MODE=$("$_BRAIN_CONFIG_BIN" get artifacts_sync_mode 2>/dev/null || echo off)

  case "$_GBRAIN_MCP_TYPE" in

fi

if [ -f "$_BRAIN_REMOTE_FILE" ] && [ ! -d "$_GSTACK_HOME/.git" ] && [ "$_BRAIN_SYNC_MODE" = "off" ]; then
```

## Model-Specific Behavioral Patch (claude)

The following nudges are tuned for the claude model family. They are
**subordinate** to skill workflow, STOP points, AskUserQuestion gates, plan-mode
safety, and /ship review gates. If a nudge below conflicts with skill instructions,
the skill wins. Treat these as preferences, not rules.

**Todo-list discipline.** When working through a multi-step plan, mark each task
complete individually as you finish it. Do not batch-complete at the end. If a task
turns out to be unnecessary, mark it skipped with a one-line reason.

**Think before heavy actions.** For complex operations (refactors, migrations,
non-trivial new features), briefly state your approach before executing. This lets
the user course-correct cheaply instead of mid-flight.

**Dedicated tools over Bash.** Prefer Read, Edit, Write, Glob, Grep over shell
equivalents (cat, sed, find, grep). The dedicated tools are cheaper and clearer.

## Voice

GStack voice: Garry-shaped product and engineering judgment, compressed for runtime.

- Lead with the point. Say what it does, why it matters, and what changes for the builder.
- Be concrete. Name files, functions, line numbers, commands, outputs, evals, and real numbers.
- Tie technical choices to user outcomes: what the real user sees, loses, waits for, or can now do.
- Be direct about quality. Bugs matter. Edge cases matter. Fix the whole thing, not the demo path.
- Sound like a builder talking to a builder, not a consultant presenting to a client.
- Never corporate, academic, PR, or hype. Avoid filler, throat-clearing, generic optimism, and founder cosplay.
- No em dashes. No AI vocabulary: delve, crucial, robust, comprehensive, nuanced, multifaceted, furthermore, moreover, additionally, pivotal, landscape, tapestry, underscore, foster, showcase, intricate, vibrant, fundamental, significant.
- The user has context you do not: domain knowledge, timing, relationships, taste. Cross-model agreement is a recommendation, not a decision. The user decides.

Good: "auth.ts:47 returns undefined when the session cookie expires. Users hit a white screen. Fix: add a null check and redirect to /login. Two lines."
Bad: "I've identified a potential issue in the authentication flow that may cause problems under certain conditions."

## Writing Style (skip entirely if `EXPLAIN_LEVEL: terse` appears in the preamble echo OR the user's current message explicitly requests terse / no-explanations output)

Applies to AskUserQuestion, user replies, and findings. AskUserQuestion Format is structure; this is prose quality.

- Gloss curated jargon on first use per skill invocation, even if the user pasted the term.
- Frame questions in outcome terms: what pain is avoided, what capability unlocks, what user experience changes.
- Use short sentences, concrete nouns, active voice.
- Close decisions with user impact: what the user sees, waits for, loses, or gains.
- User-turn override wins: if the current message asks for terse / no explanations / just the answer, skip this section.
- Terse mode (EXPLAIN_LEVEL: terse): no glosses, no outcome-framing layer, shorter responses.

Curated jargon list lives at `~/.claude/skills/gstack/scripts/jargon-list.json` (80+ terms). On the first jargon term you encounter this session, Read that file once; treat the `terms` array as the canonical list. The list is repo-owned and may grow between releases.


## Completeness Principle — Boil the Ocean

AI makes completeness cheap, so the complete thing is the goal. Recommend full coverage (tests, edge cases, error paths) — boil the ocean one lake at a time. The only thing out of scope is genuinely unrelated work (rewrites, multi-quarter migrations); flag that as separate scope, never as an excuse for a shortcut.

When options differ in coverage, include `Completeness: X/10` (10 = all edge cases, 7 = happy path, 3 = shortcut). When options differ in kind, write: `Note: options differ in kind, not coverage — no completeness score.` Do not fabricate scores.

## Confusion Protocol

For high-stakes ambiguity (architecture, data model, destructive scope, missing context), STOP. Name it in one sentence, present 2-3 options with tradeoffs, and ask. Do not use for routine coding or obvious changes.

Before each AskUserQuestion, choose `question_id` from `scripts/question-registry.ts` or `{skill}-{slug}`, then run `~/.claude/skills/gstack/bin/gstack-question-preference --check "<id>"`. `AUTO_DECIDE` means choose the recommended option and say "Auto-decided [summary] → [option] (your preference). Change with /plan-tune." `ASK_NORMALLY` means ask.

**Embed the question_id as a marker in the question text** so hooks can identify it deterministically (plan-tune cathedral T14 / D18 progressive markers). Append `<gstack-qid:{question_id}>` somewhere in the rendered question (the leading line or trailing line is fine; the marker doesn't render visibly to the user when wrapped in HTML-style angle brackets, but the hook strips it). Without the marker the PreToolUse enforcement hook treats the AUQ as observed-only and never auto-decides — so always include it when the question matches a registered `question_id`.

**Embed the option recommendation via the `(recommended)` label suffix** on exactly one option per AUQ. The PreToolUse hook parses `(recommended)` first, falls back to "Recommendation: X" prose, and refuses to auto-decide if ambiguous. Two `(recommended)` labels = refuse.

## Step 0: Detect platform and base branch

First, detect the git hosting platform from the remote URL:

```bash
git remote get-url origin 2>/dev/null
```

- If the URL contains "github.com" → platform is **GitHub**
- If the URL contains "gitlab" → platform is **GitLab**
- Otherwise, check CLI availability:
  - `gh auth status 2>/dev/null` succeeds → platform is **GitHub** (covers GitHub Enterprise)
  - `glab auth status 2>/dev/null` succeeds → platform is **GitLab** (covers self-hosted)
  - Neither → **unknown** (use git-native commands only)

PR/MR exists. Use the result as "the base branch" in all subsequent steps.

**If GitHub:**
1. `gh pr view --json baseRefName -q .baseRefName` — if succeeds, use it
2. `gh repo view --json defaultBranchRef -q .defaultBranchRef.name` — if succeeds, use it

**If GitLab:**
1. `glab mr view -F json 2>/dev/null` and extract the `target_branch` field — if succeeds, use it
2. `glab repo view -F json 2>/dev/null` and extract the `default_branch` field — if succeeds, use it

**Git-native fallback (if unknown platform, or CLI commands fail):**
1. `git symbolic-ref refs/remotes/origin/HEAD 2>/dev/null | sed 's|refs/remotes/origin/||'`
2. If that fails: `git rev-parse --verify origin/main 2>/dev/null` → use `main`
3. If that fails: `git rev-parse --verify origin/master 2>/dev/null` → use `master`

If all fail, fall back to `main`.

Print the detected base branch name. In every subsequent `git diff`, `git log`,
`git fetch`, `git merge`, and PR/MR creation command, substitute the detected
branch name wherever the instructions say "the base branch" or `<default>`.

# /autoplan — Auto-Review Pipeline

One command. Rough plan in, fully reviewed plan out.

/autoplan reads the full CEO, design, eng, and DX review skill files from disk and follows
them at full depth — same rigor, same sections, same methodology as running each skill
manually. The only difference: intermediate AskUserQuestion calls are auto-decided using
the 6 principles below. Taste decisions (where reasonable people could disagree) are
surfaced at a final approval gate.

---

## The 6 Decision Principles

These rules auto-answer every intermediate question:

1. **Choose completeness** — Ship the whole thing. Pick the approach that covers more edge cases.
2. **Boil lakes** — Fix everything in the blast radius (files modified by this plan + direct importers). Auto-approve expansions that are in blast radius AND < 1 day CC effort (< 5 files, no new infra).
3. **Pragmatic** — If two options fix the same thing, pick the cleaner one. 5 seconds choosing, not 5 minutes.
4. **DRY** — Duplicates existing functionality? Reject. Reuse what exists.
5. **Explicit over clever** — 10-line obvious fix > 200-line abstraction. Pick what a new contributor reads in 30 seconds.
6. **Bias toward action** — Merge > review cycles > stale deliberation. Flag concerns but don't block.

**Conflict resolution (context-dependent tiebreakers):**
- **CEO phase:** P1 (completeness) + P2 (boil lakes) dominate.
- **Eng phase:** P5 (explicit) + P3 (pragmatic) dominate.
- **Design phase:** P5 (explicit) + P1 (completeness) dominate.

---

## Decision Classification

Every auto-decision is classified:

**Mechanical** — one clearly right answer. Auto-decide silently.
Examples: run codex (always yes), run evals (always yes), reduce scope on a complete plan (always no).

**Taste** — reasonable people could disagree. Auto-decide with recommendation, but surface at the final gate. Three natural sources:
1. **Close approaches** — top two are both viable with different tradeoffs.
2. **Borderline scope** — in blast radius but 3-5 files, or ambiguous radius.
3. **Codex disagreements** — codex recommends differently and has a valid point.

**User Challenge** — both models agree the user's stated direction should change.
This is qualitatively different from taste decisions. When Claude and Codex both
recommend merging, splitting, adding, or removing features/skills/workflows that
the user specified, this is a User Challenge. It is NEVER auto-decided.

User Challenges go to the final approval gate with richer context than taste
decisions:
- **What the user said:** (their original direction)
- **What both models recommend:** (the change)
- **Why:** (the models' reasoning)
- **What context we might be missing:** (explicit acknowledgment of blind spots)
- **If we're wrong, the cost is:** (what happens if the user's original direction
  was right and we changed it)

The user's original direction is the default. The models must make the case for
change, not the other way around.

**Exception:** If both models flag the change as a security vulnerability or
feasibility blocker (not a preference), the AskUserQuestion framing explicitly
warns: "Both models believe this is a security/feasibility risk, not just a
preference." The user still decides, but the framing is appropriately urgent.

---

## Sequential Execution — MANDATORY

Phases MUST execute in strict order: CEO → Design → Eng → DX.
Each phase MUST complete fully before the next begins.
NEVER run phases in parallel — each builds on the previous.

Between each phase, emit a phase-transition summary and verify that all required
outputs from the prior phase are written before starting the next.

---

## What "Auto-Decide" Means

Auto-decide replaces the USER'S judgment with the 6 principles. It does NOT replace
the ANALYSIS. Every section in the loaded skill files must still be executed at the
same depth as the interactive version. The only thing that changes is who answers the
AskUserQuestion: you do, using the 6 principles, instead of the user.

**Two exceptions — never auto-decided:**
1. Premises (Phase 1) — require human judgment about what problem to solve.
2. User Challenges — when both models agree the user's stated direction should change
   (merge, split, add, remove features/workflows). The user always has context models
   lack. See Decision Classification above.

**You MUST still:**
- READ the actual code, diffs, and files each section references
- PRODUCE every output the section requires (diagrams, tables, registries, artifacts)
- IDENTIFY every issue the section is designed to catch
- DECIDE each issue using the 6 principles (instead of asking the user)
- LOG each decision in the audit trail
- WRITE all required artifacts to disk

**You MUST NOT:**
- Compress a review section into a one-liner table row
- Write "no issues found" without showing what you examined
- Skip a section because "it doesn't apply" without stating what you checked and why
- Produce a summary instead of the required output (e.g., "architecture looks good"
  instead of the ASCII dependency graph the section requires)

"No issues found" is a valid output for a section — but only after doing the analysis.
State what you examined and why nothing was flagged (1-2 sentences minimum).
"Skipped" is never valid for a non-skip-listed section.

## Implementation Tasks aggregator

Before rendering the Final Approval Gate output block below, aggregate the
per-phase task lists each review skill wrote.

```bash
eval "$(~/.claude/skills/gstack/bin/gstack-slug 2>/dev/null)"
TASKS_DIR="${HOME}/.gstack/projects/${SLUG:-unknown}"
BRANCH=$(git branch --show-current 2>/dev/null || echo unknown)
# Commit window: last 5 commits on this branch. Drops stale standalone reviews.
COMMITS_RECENT=$(git log --format=%H -n 5 2>/dev/null | tr '\n' '|' | sed 's/|$//')

AGGREGATED_TASKS=""
if command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  # Collect entries from all 4 phases, scoped to current branch + commit window.
  # For each phase, keep only the latest run_id. Within the surviving set,
  # dedupe by (component, sorted(files), title) — exact match only.
  # Sort by priority (P1 > P2 > P3) then by phase order.
  ALL_JSONL=$(mktemp -t autoplan-tasks.XXXXXXXX)
  for phase in ceo-review design-review eng-review devex-review; do
    # Use find instead of glob expansion — zsh nomatch errors otherwise when
    # a phase produced no JSONL files. Sorting by name keeps the order stable.
    while IFS= read -r f; do
      [ -f "$f" ] || continue
      # Filter to current branch + recent commits, then keep records for the
      # latest run_id only. (Single phase may have multiple files if the user
      # re-ran the review; aggregator takes the newest.)
      jq -c --arg branch "$BRANCH" --arg commits "$COMMITS_RECENT" \
        'select(.branch == $branch and ($commits | split("|") | index(.commit) != null))' \
        "$f" 2>/dev/null >> "$ALL_JSONL" || true
    done < <(find "$TASKS_DIR" -maxdepth 1 -name "tasks-$phase-*.jsonl" 2>/dev/null | sort)
    # Reduce to latest run_id per phase
    if [ -s "$ALL_JSONL" ]; then
      jq -sc --arg phase "$phase" \
        '[.[] | select(.phase == $phase)] | (max_by(.run_id) // null) as $latest_run | if $latest_run then map(select(.run_id == $latest_run.run_id)) else [] end | .[]' \
        "$ALL_JSONL" > "$ALL_JSONL.phase" 2>/dev/null || true
      # Replace with reduced version for this phase, accumulating others
      jq -c --arg phase "$phase" 'select(.phase != $phase)' "$ALL_JSONL" > "$ALL_JSONL.other" 2>/dev/null || true
      cat "$ALL_JSONL.other" "$ALL_JSONL.phase" > "$ALL_JSONL"
      rm -f "$ALL_JSONL.phase" "$ALL_JSONL.other"
    fi
  done

  # Exact-match dedup by (component, sorted(files), title). Non-matches kept
  # separately with a possible-duplicate marker injected by the renderer.
  AGGREGATED_TASKS=$(jq -s \
    'group_by([.component, (.files | sort), .title])
     | map(
         # Take the highest-priority entry per group; tie-break by phase order
         sort_by({P1:0,P2:1,P3:2}[.priority] // 99, {"ceo-review":0,"design-review":1,"eng-review":2,"devex-review":3}[.phase] // 99) | .[0]
       )
     | sort_by({P1:0,P2:1,P3:2}[.priority] // 99, {"ceo-review":0,"design-review":1,"eng-review":2,"devex-review":3}[.phase] // 99)
     | if length == 0 then "_No actionable tasks emitted from any phase._" else
         map("- [ ] **\(.id) (\(.priority), human: \(.effort_human) / CC: \(.effort_cc)) — \(.component)** — \(.title)\n  - Surfaced by: \(.phase) — \(.source_finding)\n  - Files: \(.files | join(", "))") | join("\n")
       end' "$ALL_JSONL" 2>/dev/null | sed 's/^"//;s/"$//;s/\\n/\n/g')
  rm -f "$ALL_JSONL"
else
  AGGREGATED_TASKS="_jq not installed — install jq to aggregate per-phase task lists. Skipping._"
fi
```

"Full depth" means: read the code the section asks you to read, produce the outputs the section requires, identify every issue, and decide each one. A one-sentence summary of a section is not "full depth" — it is a skip. If you catch yourself writing fewer than 3 sentences for any review section, you are likely compressing.
- **Artifacts are deliverables.** Test plan artifact, failure modes registry, error/rescue table, ASCII diagrams — these must exist on disk or in the plan file when the review completes. If they don't exist, the review is incomplete.
- **Sequential order.** CEO → Design → Eng → DX. Each phase builds on the last.

47	  /// The working directory is supplied to the executor (`run(in:)`), not as a claude flag.
48	  /// `systemPrompt`, when given, replaces claude's heavy default system prompt — it both shapes the
49	  /// output and cuts token cost (task #15). `model`, when given, pins a cheap/fast model so the
50	  /// diagnosis doesn't run on the user's (often Opus) default. The prompt stays the trailing positional.
51	  static func claudeInline(systemPrompt: String? = nil, model: String? = nil, prompt: String)
52	    -> AgentInvocation
53	  {
54	    var arguments = [
55	      "--print",
56	      "--output-format", "json",
57	      "--permission-mode", "plan",
58	      "--allowed-tools", "none",
59	      "--no-session-persistence",
60	    ]
61	    if let model, !model.isEmpty {
62	      arguments.append(contentsOf: ["--model", model])
63	    }
64	    if let systemPrompt, !systemPrompt.isEmpty {
65	      arguments.append(contentsOf: ["--system-prompt", systemPrompt])
66	    }
67	    arguments.append(prompt)
68	    return AgentInvocation(executable: AgentBackend.claude.executable, arguments: arguments)
69	  }
70	}

72	/// The raw outcome of an inline diagnosis run, before the model's text is parsed into an
73	/// `AgentDiagnosis` (T5). Distinct cases so the banner can show actionable states (X1/A2).
74	enum AgentRunOutcome: Sendable, Equatable {
75	  /// Process succeeded; `stdout` is the raw JSON envelope (claude `--output-format json`).
76	  case success(stdout: String)
77	  /// `/usr/bin/env` exit 127 — the agent CLI isn't on PATH.
78	  case cliNotFound
79	  /// Non-zero exit whose output looks like an auth/login failure.
80	  case notAuthenticated
81	  /// The timeout fired.
82	  case timedOut
83	  /// Succeeded but produced no usable text.
84	  case emptyOutput
85	  /// Any other non-zero exit (stderr tail kept for the banner / logs).
86	  case failed(exitCode: Int32, stderr: String)
87	}
88	
89	/// A seam (mirrors `StatusCommandRunning`) so the inline-agent manager (T6) is unit-testable with a
90	/// fake runner — no real `claude`/`codex` process.
91	protocol AgentRunning: Sendable {
92	  /// Run an inline, no-tools diagnosis (claude only, X1). `systemPrompt` replaces claude's default
93	  /// to shape output + cut cost; `model` pins a cheap/fast model (task #15). `cwd` is where claude
94	  /// runs — callers should pass a NEUTRAL dir (not the project) so `CLAUDE.md` doesn't auto-load:
95	  /// the inline path has no tools and gets all context from `prompt`, so the real failure cwd
96	  /// belongs in the prompt text, not here.
97	  func diagnoseInline(
98	    systemPrompt: String?, model: String?, prompt: String, cwd: String, timeout: TimeInterval
99	  ) async -> AgentRunOutcome
100	}
101	
102	/// Default `AgentRunning`: builds the claude inline argv and runs it through the existing
103	/// `StatusCommandRunning` executor (CQ1 — no duplicated process/drain/timeout/cancel code). The
104	/// executor's process-group termination (X2, T3) reaps any agent child processes on cancel/timeout.
105	struct AgentRunner: AgentRunning {
106	  let executor: StatusCommandRunning
107	
108	  init(executor: StatusCommandRunning = StatusCommandRunner()) {
109	    self.executor = executor
110	  }
111	
112	  func diagnoseInline(
113	    systemPrompt: String? = nil, model: String? = nil, prompt: String, cwd: String,
114	    timeout: TimeInterval = 60
115	  ) async -> AgentRunOutcome {
116	    let invocation = AgentInvocationBuilder.claudeInline(
117	      systemPrompt: systemPrompt, model: model, prompt: prompt)
118	    let result = await executor.run(
119	      invocation.executable, invocation.arguments, in: cwd, timeout: timeout)
120	    return Self.classify(result)
121	  }
122	
123	  /// Map a raw process result to a diagnosis outcome. Pure + unit-tested. stdout carries the model's
124	  /// JSON; stderr is treated only as diagnostics (CLI warnings must not be mistaken for the result).
125	  static func classify(_ result: CommandResult) -> AgentRunOutcome {
126	    if result.timedOut { return .timedOut }
127	    if result.exitCode == CommandResult.commandNotFound { return .cliNotFound }
128	    if result.exitCode != 0 {
129	      if isAuthFailure(result.stderr + "\n" + result.stdout) {
130	        return .notAuthenticated
131	      }
132	      return .failed(exitCode: result.exitCode, stderr: String(result.stderr.suffix(2000)))
133	    }
134	    return result.stdout.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespacesAndNewlines).isEmpty
135	      ? .emptyOutput
136	      : .success(stdout: result.stdout)
137	  }
138	
139	  /// Heuristic auth/login-failure detection over the agent CLI's combined output.
140	  static func isAuthFailure(_ text: String) -> Bool {
141	    let lowered = text.lowercased()
142	    return [
143	      "not authenticated", "unauthorized", "authentication", "invalid api key", "invalid_api_key",
144	      "please log in", "please login", "run `claude login`", "run claude login", "no api key",
145	    ].contains { lowered.contains($0) }
146	  }
147	}

4	/// A captured failed command, ready to diagnose (issue #49). The host builds this from the surface
5	/// view (command + cwd from shell integration, exit code from `command_finished`, `output` from
6	/// `readCommandRegion`); passing a value type keeps `TerminalAgentManager` testable without a live
7	/// terminal. `output` is the tidied capture; the manager applies redaction before sending.
8	struct FailedCommand: Equatable, Sendable {
9	  var command: String?
10	  var cwd: String?
11	  var exitCode: Int32
12	  var shell: String?
13	  var output: String
14	  var isRunTab: Bool
15	  var isRemote: Bool
16	}
17	
18	/// Distinct error states so the banner can show actionable guidance.
19	enum AgentErrorKind: Equatable, Sendable {
20	  case cliNotFound
21	  case notAuthenticated
22	  case timedOut
23	  case emptyOutput
24	  case malformed
25	  case other(String)
26	}
27	
28	/// What the banner shows for a tab (issue #49). Absent (no entry) means no banner.
29	enum AgentBannerState: Equatable, Sendable {
30	  /// An eligible failure that hasn't been diagnosed yet — shows a "Diagnose" button.
31	  case awaitingDiagnose(FailedCommand)
32	  /// A diagnosis is running.
33	  case loading(FailedCommand)
34	  /// A diagnosis came back.
35	  case ready(FailedCommand, AgentDiagnosis)
36	  /// The run failed (CLI missing, auth, timeout, …).
37	  case failure(FailedCommand, AgentErrorKind)
38	  /// A remote/ssh/tmux session — the local agent can't see the real host, so we caveat and disable
39	  /// Investigate rather than give a confidently-wrong local diagnosis (X5).
40	  case remoteCaveat(FailedCommand)
41	
42	  /// The captured failure every state carries, plus the diagnosis when one is ready — for building
43	  /// the interactive Investigate seed prompt (issue #49).
44	  var failureAndDiagnosis: (FailedCommand, AgentDiagnosis?) {
45	    switch self {
46	    case .awaitingDiagnose(let failure), .loading(let failure), .failure(let failure, _),
47	      .remoteCaveat(let failure):
48	      return (failure, nil)
49	    case .ready(let failure, let diagnosis):
50	      return (failure, diagnosis)
51	    }
52	  }
53	}
54	
55	/// Orchestrates the inline terminal agent (issue #49, T6): classify a finished command, decide
56	/// manual vs automatic, run the diagnosis (debounced, cooldown-bounded, cancel-superseding), guard
57	/// the pane lifecycle, and publish per-tab banner state. `@MainActor` + `ObservableObject` to match
58	/// `AppStore`/`TerminalSessions`. Pure decision logic lives in `FailureClassifier`; the runner and
59	/// the feature gates are injected so the state machine is seam-tested with a fake.
60	@MainActor
61	final class TerminalAgentManager: ObservableObject {
62	  @Published private(set) var banners: [TerminalTab.ID: AgentBannerState] = [:]
63	
64	  /// Cheap gate so the host can skip the (screen-reading) capture work entirely when the feature is
65	  /// off — checked before `readCommandRegion()` runs on every command finish.
66	  var isEnabled: Bool { featureEnabled() }
67	
68	  /// The tab whose banner should show the one-time "auto-diagnose from now on?" prompt — set after
69	  /// the user's FIRST manual Diagnose (when auto is off and they haven't been asked yet). nil = no
70	  /// prompt. The banner for this tab presents it; the answer persists the choice.
71	  @Published private(set) var autoOptInPromptTab: TerminalTab.ID?
72	
73	  private let runner: AgentRunning
74	  private let featureEnabled: () -> Bool
75	  private let autoDiagnoseEnabled: () -> Bool
76	  private let redactSecrets: () -> Bool
77	  /// The model for the inline diagnosis (cheap/fast by default; nil = the CLI's own default).
78	  private let model: () -> String?
79	  /// Whether the one-time auto-diagnose opt-in prompt has already been shown.
80	  private let hasPromptedAutoOptIn: () -> Bool
81	  /// Persist the opt-in answer: always mark prompted; enable auto-diagnose when accepted.
82	  private let persistAutoOptIn: (_ enable: Bool) -> Void
83	  private let now: () -> Date
84	  private let cooldown: TimeInterval
85	  /// Where the inline (no-tools) claude call runs. A NEUTRAL dir, not the project, so `CLAUDE.md`
86	  /// doesn't auto-load and inflate cost (token opt, task #15); the real cwd is in the prompt text.
87	  private let inlineCwd: String
88	  private let timeout: TimeInterval
89	
90	  /// The in-flight diagnosis per tab — cancelling it SIGKILLs the agent process via the runner's
91	  /// cancellation handler (T3), so a superseding failure doesn't leave a stale agent running.
92	  private(set) var inFlight: [TerminalTab.ID: Task<Void, Never>] = [:]
93	  /// Last auto-fire per target, for the cooldown (P1).
94	  private var lastAutoFire: [TerminalTarget.ID: Date] = [:]
95	  /// The latest failure per tab, retained even when soft-suppressed so a manual Diagnose still works.
96	  private var lastFailure: [TerminalTab.ID: FailedCommand] = [:]
97	
98	  init(
99	    runner: AgentRunning = AgentRunner(),
100	    featureEnabled: @escaping () -> Bool = { true },
101	    autoDiagnoseEnabled: @escaping () -> Bool = { Defaults[.terminalAgentAutoDiagnose] },
102	    redactSecrets: @escaping () -> Bool = { Defaults[.terminalAgentRedactSecrets] },
103	    model: @escaping () -> String? = {
104	      let value = Defaults[.terminalAgentModel]
105	      return value.isEmpty ? nil : value
106	    },
107	    hasPromptedAutoOptIn: @escaping () -> Bool = { Defaults[.terminalAgentAutoDiagnosePrompted] },
108	    persistAutoOptIn: @escaping (Bool) -> Void = { enable in
109	      Defaults[.terminalAgentAutoDiagnosePrompted] = true
110	      if enable { Defaults[.terminalAgentAutoDiagnose] = true }
111	    },
112	    now: @escaping () -> Date = Date.init,
113	    cooldown: TimeInterval = 20,
114	    inlineCwd: String = NSTemporaryDirectory(),
115	    timeout: TimeInterval = 60
116	  ) {
117	    self.runner = runner
118	    self.featureEnabled = featureEnabled
119	    self.autoDiagnoseEnabled = autoDiagnoseEnabled
120	    self.redactSecrets = redactSecrets
121	    self.model = model
122	    self.hasPromptedAutoOptIn = hasPromptedAutoOptIn
123	    self.persistAutoOptIn = persistAutoOptIn
124	    self.now = now
125	    self.cooldown = cooldown
126	    self.inlineCwd = inlineCwd
127	    self.timeout = timeout
128	  }
129	
130	  // MARK: Events
131	
132	  /// A command finished in `tab`. `failure` is nil when the exit code is unknown / not a failure the
133	  /// host bothered to capture. Decides skip / soft-suppress / show-banner / auto-fire.
134	  func commandFinished(
135	    tab: TerminalTab.ID, target: TerminalTarget.ID, failure: FailedCommand?
136	  ) {
137	    guard featureEnabled() else { return }
138	    guard let failure else {
139	      clear(tab: tab)
140	      return
141	    }
142	
143	    let disposition = FailureClassifier.disposition(
144	      exitCode: failure.exitCode, command: failure.command, isRunTab: failure.isRunTab,
145	      hasCapture: !failure.output.isEmpty)
146	
147	    switch disposition {
148	    case .skip:
149	      clear(tab: tab)
150	    case .manualOnly:
151	      // Soft-suppress: no banner, but keep the context so a manual "Diagnose last command" works.
152	      lastFailure[tab] = failure
153	      setBanner(nil, tab: tab)
154	    case .eligible:
155	      lastFailure[tab] = failure
156	      if failure.isRemote {
157	        setBanner(.remoteCaveat(failure), tab: tab)
158	      } else if autoDiagnoseEnabled() && cooldownElapsed(target: target) {
159	        start(tab: tab, target: target, failure: failure, auto: true)
160	      } else {
161	        setBanner(.awaitingDiagnose(failure), tab: tab)
162	      }
163	    }
164	  }
165	
166	  /// Explicit Diagnose (banner button or the "Diagnose last command" menu action). Works for an
167	  /// awaiting banner and for a soft-suppressed failure.
168	  func diagnose(tab: TerminalTab.ID, target: TerminalTarget.ID) {
169	    guard let failure = currentFailure(tab: tab), !failure.isRemote else { return }
170	    start(tab: tab, target: target, failure: failure, auto: false)
171	    // First manual Diagnose (auto off, never asked) → offer to make it automatic from now on.
172	    if !autoDiagnoseEnabled() && !hasPromptedAutoOptIn() {
173	      autoOptInPromptTab = tab
174	    }
175	  }
176	
177	  /// Answer the one-time "auto-diagnose from now on?" prompt. `enable` turns auto-diagnose on;
178	  /// either way the prompt is marked shown so it never re-asks.
179	  func respondToAutoOptIn(enable: Bool) {
180	    persistAutoOptIn(enable)
181	    autoOptInPromptTab = nil
182	  }
183	
184	  /// Dismiss the banner (cancels any in-flight run).
185	  func dismiss(tab: TerminalTab.ID) {
186	    if autoOptInPromptTab == tab { autoOptInPromptTab = nil }
187	    clear(tab: tab)
188	  }
189	
190	  /// The pane/tab went away (A6): cancel in-flight, drop all state for it.
191	  func tabClosed(_ tab: TerminalTab.ID) {
192	    if autoOptInPromptTab == tab { autoOptInPromptTab = nil }
193	    clear(tab: tab)
194	    lastFailure[tab] = nil
195	  }
196	
197	  // MARK: Diagnosis
198	
199	  private func start(
200	    tab: TerminalTab.ID, target: TerminalTarget.ID, failure: FailedCommand, auto: Bool
201	  ) {
202	    inFlight[tab]?.cancel()  // cancel-supersede
203	    if auto { lastAutoFire[target] = now() }
204	    setBanner(.loading(failure), tab: tab)
205	
206	    let output = redactSecrets() ? SecretRedactor.redact(failure.output) : failure.output
207	    let prompt = AgentPrompt.userMessage(
208	      command: failure.command, cwd: failure.cwd, exitCode: failure.exitCode, shell: failure.shell,
209	      output: output)
210	    let systemPrompt = AgentPrompt.systemPrompt
211	    let runner = self.runner
212	    let cwd = inlineCwd
213	    let timeout = self.timeout
214	    let model = self.model()
215	
216	    inFlight[tab] = Task { [weak self] in
217	      let outcome = await runner.diagnoseInline(
218	        systemPrompt: systemPrompt, model: model, prompt: prompt, cwd: cwd, timeout: timeout)
219	      if Task.isCancelled { return }
220	      self?.apply(outcome: outcome, tab: tab, failure: failure)
221	    }
222	  }
223	
224	  private func apply(outcome: AgentRunOutcome, tab: TerminalTab.ID, failure: FailedCommand) {
225	    // Ignore a result whose banner was superseded or dismissed while it ran.
226	    guard case .loading(let pending)? = banners[tab], pending == failure else { return }
227	    inFlight[tab] = nil
228	
229	    let resolved: AgentBannerState
230	    switch outcome {
231	    case .success(let stdout):
232	      resolved =
233	        AgentPrompt.parse(envelopeJSON: stdout).map { .ready(failure, $0) }
234	        ?? .failure(failure, .malformed)
235	    case .cliNotFound: resolved = .failure(failure, .cliNotFound)
236	    case .notAuthenticated: resolved = .failure(failure, .notAuthenticated)
237	    case .timedOut: resolved = .failure(failure, .timedOut)
238	    case .emptyOutput: resolved = .failure(failure, .emptyOutput)
239	    case .failed(let code, _): resolved = .failure(failure, .other("exit \(code)"))
240	    }
241	
242	    setBanner(resolved, tab: tab)
243	  }
244	
245	  // MARK: Helpers
246	
247	  private func clear(tab: TerminalTab.ID) {
248	    inFlight[tab]?.cancel()
249	    inFlight[tab] = nil
250	    setBanner(nil, tab: tab)
251	  }
252	
253	  private func setBanner(_ state: AgentBannerState?, tab: TerminalTab.ID) {
254	    banners[tab] = state
255	  }
256	
257	  private func cooldownElapsed(target: TerminalTarget.ID) -> Bool {
258	    guard let last = lastAutoFire[target] else { return true }
259	    return now().timeIntervalSince(last) >= cooldown
260	  }
261	
262	  private func currentFailure(tab: TerminalTab.ID) -> FailedCommand? {
263	    if case .awaitingDiagnose(let failure)? = banners[tab] { return failure }
264	    return lastFailure[tab]
265	  }
266	}

11	/// hit-testing, so overlay buttons silently swallow clicks; a popover lives in its own window.

input.content:
# Issue #145 — Offer to resume an agent session in a restored pane

## Context

After #46 a restored pane is inert: right workroom, right directory, dead shell. If you were
mid-conversation with Claude or Codex, that conversation still exists in the agent's own store.
#145 offers a one-click route back to it, at restore time only, spawning nothing at launch.

The issue is already well specified. This plan does three things the issue does not: it **corrects
four factual claims** that turn out to be wrong or incomplete against the actual code and the actual
agent stores on disk, it **makes three decisions the issue left implicit**, and it sequences the
work.

---

## Verified facts (checked 2026-08-09, not assumed)

| Claim in #145 | Verdict | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| libghostty exposes no child pid / pty fd | ✅ **true** | `DerivedData/Build/Products/Release/include/ghostty.h` — the only child-process symbol is `ghostty_surface_message_childexited_s` (line 824). No pid, no fd. |
| Codex rollout line 1 is a `session_meta` record carrying `cwd` | ✅ **true** | `head -1` of a real rollout: `{payload, timestamp, type}`, `type == "session_meta"`, `payload` has `cwd`. |
| Codex sessions live at `~/.codex/sessions/YYYY/MM/DD/rollout-*.jsonl` | ✅ **true** | Verified 2026/03…2026/08 date tree. |
| `claude --resume` is a picker; `--continue` resumes in-cwd | ✅ **true** | `claude --help`: `-r, --resume [value]`, `-c, --continue`. |
| `codex resume` is a picker; `--last` skips it | ✅ **true** | `codex resume --help`: "picker by default; use `--last` to continue the most recent". |
| `TerminalAgentBanner` + `AgentBannerViewModel` exist, reuse them | ⚠️ **half true** | They exist. But see **C1** and **C2** — reusing them as-is is a bug, not a shortcut. |
| Claude slug = cwd with `/` replaced by `-` | ❌ **WRONG** | See **C3**. `.` is also replaced. |
| `SessionFile.savedAt` "gives the recency window with no new state" | ❌ **WRONG** | See **C4**. It is persisted but thrown away at load. |

### C1 — `AgentBannerState` is failure-shaped, and there is one slot per tab

`AgentBannerState` (`Core/TerminalAgentManager.swift:29`) has five cases and **every one carries a
`FailedCommand`**. Its accessor is not optional:

```swift
var failureAndDiagnosis: (FailedCommand, AgentDiagnosis?)
```

`AgentPrompt.investigateCommandLine(for:)` destructures that non-optional tuple. A resume offer has
no failed command, so adding a sixth case forces either a fake `FailedCommand` (lying to the
Investigate path) or a signature change with a real call-site.

Worse, the store is single-slot:

```swift
@Published private(set) var banners: [TerminalTab.ID: AgentBannerState] = [:]
```

So a resume offer and a diagnosis **evict each other**. Concretely, with the issue's design as
written: restored pane shows *Resume Claude…*; the user runs `npm test`; it fails;
`commandFinished` calls `setBanner(.awaitingDiagnose(...))` and the resume offer is gone for good.
The reverse also happens — discovery is async by design, so a late offer can stomp a live
`.loading` diagnosis mid-run.

**This is the single biggest thing the issue gets wrong.** "Reuse it" reads as free; it is not.

### C2 — The "banner" is a red status-bar chip behind a popover

`TerminalStatusBar.swift:9` is explicit: *"The diagnosis is a compact indicator that opens the full
`TerminalAgentBanner` in a POPOVER — not an overlay"* (a SwiftUI overlay loses hit-testing to the
terminal's Metal `NSView`). The chip is tinted by `diagnosisTint`, which maps `.awaiting` to
`theme.tokens.failure` — **red** — with `.help("Show the agent's diagnosis")` and a tab-strip badge
at `TerminalTabStrip.swift:149`.

Rendering a Resume offer through that path produces a red, failure-coloured chip labelled as a
diagnosis, that you must click to discover an offer you never asked for. Wrong on colour semantics,
wrong on tooltip, wrong on discoverability for the one affordance whose entire job is to be noticed
in the first ten seconds after launch.

### C3 — The Claude slug replaces `.` as well as `/`

Verified against 58 real project directories:

| Directory on disk | Real path |
|---|---|
| `-Users-joelmoss--buzz` | `/Users/joelmoss/.buzz` (confirmed to exist) |
| `-Users-joelmoss--superconductor-worktrees-platform-sc-…` | `/Users/joelmoss/.superconductor/worktrees/…` |
| `-Users-joelmoss-dev-clients-…-platform--claude-worktrees-…` | `…/platform/.claude/worktrees/…` |

A single leading `.` becomes a second `-`. Implementing the issue's stated rule verbatim means any
workroom path containing a dot — `~/.local/...`, a workroom branch named `v2.0`, a `.worktrees`
directory — silently produces a wrong slug and **never offers the button**, with no error and no
way to tell it apart from "no history here".

`_` is unverified: no underscore path exists in this store. **Do not guess it.** T1 below is a
two-minute spike that settles it empirically.

This also strengthens the issue's own collision argument, and the plan keeps its conclusion: the
scheme is Claude's, we mirror it, we do not invent our own.

### C4 — `savedAt` is persisted but discarded at load

`ProjectStore.loadSessionIfNeeded` (`ProjectStore.swift:209`) keeps only the windows:

```swift
guard case .restored(let file, _) = sessionCoordinator.read() else { return }
unclaimedSessionWindows = file.windows
```

`file.savedAt` is dropped on the floor. The issue's "no new state" claim is true of the *file
format* (nothing new is written) but false of the runtime: `savedAt` needs a stored property on
`ProjectStore` and a read path out to whatever does discovery. Small, but it is a real edit in a
file the issue's Files Reference does not list.

### C5 — Restored panes are not marked, and the mark must be per-tab

`TerminalSessions.restore` (`:601`) builds tabs through the same `makeTerminalTab` that `addTab`
(⌘T) uses. Nothing afterwards distinguishes them. The issue's eligibility rule ("only panes created
by `restore` during this launch") therefore needs a new field.

It must be **per tab**, not a launch-scoped flag: acceptance criterion 4 and testing-plan row 7 both
require that a ⌘T pane opened in a restored target does *not* qualify. `TerminalTab` is a struct
with `let id = UUID()`, so `var wasRestored: Bool = false` is a one-line, value-typed addition that
copies correctly through every existing mutation path.

---

## The three decisions the issue left open

### D1 — Where the offer lives

**Decision: a separate `resumeOffers: [TerminalTab.ID: [AgentBackend]]` on `TerminalAgentManager`,
rendered as its own status-bar segment.** Not a sixth `AgentBannerState` case.

Rationale: it is the only option that survives C1. The two states are genuinely independent — a
restored pane can have a resume offer *and* then fail a command — so they need two slots. It also
sidesteps C2 for free: a separate segment gets its own tint (accent, not failure), its own tooltip,
and can render as a direct button rather than a popover, because a resume offer has no body to
show — it is one click.

Cost: `TerminalStatusBar` gains a second agent-ish segment. Acceptable; it is ~20 lines and the bar
already composes five segments.

Rejected: a sixth `AgentBannerState` case. Forces `failureAndDiagnosis` to go optional, breaks the
Investigate call site, and still leaves the two states fighting over one dictionary slot.

### D2 — How the resume command runs

This is the real taste call, and both options are defensible.

**(a) Type into the restored pane's live shell** — the issue's design. Keeps the restored pane
meaningful, which is the emotional point of the feature. Two costs: it inverts #49's explicit
"we never auto-execute" policy on `sendText` (`GhosttySurfaceView.swift:970`), and — unaddressed by
the issue — **the shell's input line may not be empty**. Discovery is async; the user may have typed
half a command by the time the offer lands and they click it. Typing `claude --resume\r` onto a
dirty line runs the wrong thing. Mitigation is either a fresh `sendText("\u{15}")` (Ctrl-U kill-line,
destroys what they typed and is shell-dependent) or accepting the risk.

**(b) `sessions.addRunTab(for:command:cwd:)`** — the vehicle the codebase *already uses* for exactly
this shape of action. `TerminalStatusBar.swift:275`'s Investigate button opens an interactive
`claude '<prompt>'` in a run tab today. No policy inversion, no dirty-line hazard, the process is
tracked by `AppStore.RunState` and `WindowRegistry.runOwner`, and the restored pane keeps its #144
replayed scrollback visible beside the live agent instead of scrolling it away.

**Recommendation: (b).** It is DRY against a precedent that already shipped, it removes two whole
risk classes, and #46's ban on run tabs is about *launch-time auto-spawn*, not user-initiated ones —
this spawns on a click, which is the same gate Investigate passes.

Flagged for the user because it visibly changes the feature: you get a new pane beside the restored
one rather than the restored pane coming alive.

### D3 — The recency window

**Decision: 24 hours, not ±300 s.**

The issue's ±5 minutes assumes the agent wrote to its session file just before you quit. Claude
appends as the conversation proceeds, so mtime is the last *message*, not the last moment the
session was alive. Leave Claude sitting idle at its prompt for ten minutes and quit — a completely
ordinary way to end a day — and mtime lands 600 s before `savedAt`, outside the window, and the
button never appears. That is a false negative on the feature's headline case.

Widening costs almost nothing, because **nothing auto-resumes**. The window's only job is to keep
the button off directories you have not touched in months; the picker still makes you choose. 24 h
keeps that property and stops the common case failing.

Keep symmetry (future-dated mtimes qualify — clock skew is real). Keep the three-day cap on Codex
date-directory scanning, widened to match: `savedAt ± 24 h` spans at most three day directories.

---

## Design

```
  launch ─▶ ProjectStore.loadSessionIfNeeded
                │  (C4) now also retains file.savedAt
                ▼
        AppStore.restorePersistedSessionIfPending
                │
                ▼
        TerminalSessions.restore  ──▶ tab.wasRestored = true   (C5)
                │
                ▼
        for each restored TERMINAL tab, off the main actor:
                │
                ├── Claude:  ~/.claude/projects/<slug(cwd)>/*.jsonl        depth 1
                │            slug: '/' and '.' → '-'   (C3, pending T1 for '_')
                │
                └── Codex:   ~/.codex/sessions/YYYY/MM/DD/rollout-*.jsonl
                             day dirs intersecting [savedAt-24h, savedAt+24h]
                             first line → JSON → .payload.cwd, ≤64KB else skip
                │
                ▼
        back on the main actor, IF the tab id still exists:
                agentManager.resumeOffers[tabID] = [.claude, .codex]     (D1)
                │
                ▼
        TerminalStatusBar: accent-tinted "Resume Claude…" / "Resume Codex…"
                │  click
                ▼
        sessions.addRunTab(for:, command: "<exe> <picker-args>", cwd:)   (D2b)
```

### Path matching

One normalizer, used on both sides:

```swift
nonisolated static func normalized(_ path: String) -> String
```

`URL(fileURLWithPath:).resolvingSymlinksInPath()`, drop a trailing slash, lowercase for comparison
(the default APFS volume is case-insensitive, so `/Users/x/Dev` and `/Users/x/dev` are one
directory). Applied to the pane cwd before slugging, and to the Codex `session_meta.cwd` before
comparing. The Claude side compares slugs, not paths, so the normalizer runs before the slug
transform, never after.

### Argv

Picker form only, built as data, never string-interpolated from anything read off disk:

```swift
static func resume(_ backend: AgentBackend) -> AgentInvocation
// .claude → AgentInvocation(executable: "claude", arguments: ["--resume"])
// .codex  → AgentInvocation(executable: "codex",  arguments: ["resume"])
```

Lives in `AgentInvocationBuilder` beside `claudeInline`. The only variable is
`AgentBackend.executable`, which is a `rawValue` on a two-case enum — nothing from disk reaches the
command line. `--continue` and `--last` appear nowhere; a unit test asserts their absence in the
built argv, and a grep gate covers the rest of the tree (AC 6).

### Threading

Discovery is file IO: a detached `Task` per restored terminal tab, results delivered back on the
main actor. Cancelled when the pane closes. Per the #144 lesson recorded in
`macapp-cli-shellout-cooperative-pool` and `macapp-history-loads-forever-gcd`, blocking file work
must not starve the cooperative pool — batch all panes' discovery into **one** background unit that
publishes once, rather than N concurrent tasks racing the launch path.

A slow or huge session directory delays the button, never the pane. Result dropped only if the tab
id is gone; selection changing is irrelevant (a background pane keeps its offer).

---

## Build sequence

Every step ends with `make app-format` + `make app-lint`; new files need `make app-generate`.

- **T1 (spike, 2 min)** — settle the `_` question in the Claude slug. `mkdir /tmp/wr_slug_probe &&
  cd it && claude -p 'hi' --allowed-tools none --permission-mode plan`, then read the directory name
  under `~/.claude/projects/`. Encode the answer in `ClaudeSessionStore.slug` with the evidence in a
  comment. **Do this first** — every other Claude-side test depends on the transform being right.
- **T2** — `Core/AgentSessionDiscovery.swift` (new). Pure slug + normalizer + recency predicate +
  Codex `session_meta` parse. No IO in the pure layer; a thin `discover(cwd:savedAt:)` on top.
- **T3** — `AgentInvocationBuilder.resume(_:)` + the argv tests.
- **T4** — `TerminalTab.wasRestored` (C5) and the one assignment in `TerminalSessions.restore`.
- **T5** — `ProjectStore` retains `savedAt` (C4) and exposes it; `AppStore+Session` kicks discovery
  for restored terminal tabs at the end of `restorePersistedSessionIfPending`.
- **T6** — `TerminalAgentManager.resumeOffers` (D1) + `tabClosed` clearing it.
- **T7** — `TerminalStatusBar` resume segment: accent tint, per-agent buttons, `.help(…)` on each
  (house rule: every control gets a tooltip), a11y ids `terminal.statusBar.resume.claude` /
  `.resume.codex`. Click → `addRunTab` (D2b).
- **T8** — `UITestFixture.agentSessionRoot` via the existing `text(_:)` seam, default-off exactly
  like `sessionFilePath`. With no path supplied, discovery is a **no-op in fixture mode** — the 34
  existing UI tests must never read the developer's real `~/.claude`.
- **T9** — tests (below).
- **T10** — docs: `macapp/README.md` line for the new file; strike nothing (no comment is falsified
  by this change).

### Files

**New:** `Core/AgentSessionDiscovery.swift`, `WorkroomAppTests/AgentSessionDiscoveryTests.swift`,
`WorkroomAppTests/AgentResumeInvocationTests.swift`.

**Modified:** `Core/AgentRunner.swift`, `Core/TerminalAgentManager.swift`,
`Core/TerminalSessions.swift`, `Core/ProjectStore.swift`, `Core/AppStore+Session.swift`,
`Core/UITestFixture.swift`, `Views/TerminalStatusBar.swift`, `macapp/README.md`.

The issue's Files Reference misses `ProjectStore.swift` (C4), `TerminalSessions.swift` (C5) and
`UITestFixture.swift`, and names `Views/TerminalAgentBanner.swift`, which D1 leaves untouched.

---

## Verification

### Unit (`macapp/WorkroomAppTests/`)

- **`AgentSessionDiscoveryTests`**
  - slug: plain path; path with `-`; path with `.` (the C3 regression — `/Users/x/.buzz` →
    `-Users-x--buzz`); path with `_` (pinned to T1's answer); the documented `/a-b/c` vs `/a/b/c`
    collision, asserted as *accepted*, not fixed.
  - normalizer: symlink resolved, trailing slash dropped, case-insensitive match.
  - recency: inside, outside, and both 24 h boundaries; a future-dated mtime qualifies.
  - Codex `session_meta`: valid cwd parsed; malformed JSON, empty file, non-JSON first line, and a
    first line over 64 KB all ignored without throwing.
  - a missing / unreadable session root yields no offers and no error (AC 7).
- **`AgentResumeInvocationTests`** — `.claude` → `["--resume"]`, `.codex` → `["resume"]`; neither
  argv contains `--continue` or `--last`; both agents qualifying yields two offers, not one guess.
- **`TerminalSessionsTests`** — `restore` marks `wasRestored`; `addTab` does not (AC 4, C5).
- **`TerminalAgentManagerTests`** — **the C1 regression:** a resume offer and a
  `.awaitingDiagnose` banner coexist on one tab; neither evicts the other in either order.
  `tabClosed` clears both.
- **`SessionRestoreTests`** — discovery does not run during `restore` itself (same lazy-IO rule the
  #144 sidecar test pins).

### XCUITest (`WorkroomAppUITests/AgentResumeUITests.swift`)

Seeded via `-WorkroomUITestAgentSessionRoot <abs path>`, mirroring `-WorkroomUITestSessionFile`.

1. Restored pane + seeded Claude root → *Resume Claude…* visible; process count before/after launch
   is unchanged (AC 5).
2. Seeded Codex root → *Resume Codex…*; both seeded → two independent actions (AC 2, 3).
3. No seeded root → no button, no error (AC 4, 7).

Scoped run (`make app-uitest` ignores `APP_TEST_FLAGS`, so raw `xcodebuild`):

```
cd macapp && xcodegen generate && xcodebuild -project WorkroomApp.xcodeproj \
  -scheme WorkroomAppUITests -configuration Debug -derivedDataPath DerivedData \
  -clonedSourcePackagesDirPath DerivedData/SourcePackages -destination 'platform=macOS' \
  -only-testing:WorkroomAppUITests/AgentResumeUITests test
```

Full gate: `make app-test` + `make app-lint` (AC 8). Read pass/fail from the `.xcresult` via
`xcresulttool`; Xcode 26 hides the summary. All `make app-*` need the sandbox disabled.

### Manual

Have a Claude conversation in a workroom, quit with ⌘Q, relaunch, confirm the button appears and
the picker opens. Then: a workroom whose path contains a dot (the C3 case). Then ⌘T in a restored
target and confirm it offers nothing.

---

## Failure modes

| Codepath | Realistic failure | Test | Handling | User sees |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Slug transform | `.` in path → wrong slug, silent no-button | ✅ C3 regression | Mirror Claude's real rule | — (silent before fix) |
| Banner slot | Resume offer and diagnosis evict each other | ✅ C1 regression | Separate dictionary (D1) | Offer vanishes on first failed command |
| `savedAt` | Not retained → no recency input at all | ✅ | Stored on `ProjectStore` (C4) | Button never appears |
| Recency | Idle agent before quit → false negative | ✅ boundaries | 24 h window (D3) | Button missing on the headline case |
| Eligibility | ⌘T pane offers resume | ✅ AC 4 | Per-tab `wasRestored` (C5) | Offer on a pane with no history |
| Discovery IO | Blocking read starves the launch path | ✅ (lazy-IO test) | One batched background unit | Slow launch |
| Late result | Pane closed before discovery returns | ✅ | Drop if tab id gone | — |
| Missing binary | `claude` not installed | ✅ AC 7 | Shell's own `command not found`; `AgentErrorKind.cliNotFound` deliberately **not** reused | Normal shell error |
| Fixture leak | UI tests read the real `~/.claude` | ✅ | Default-off `agentSessionRoot` (T8) | — |

**Critical gaps (no test AND no handling AND silent): 0.**

---

## NOT in scope

- **Auto-resume at launch.** Contradicts #46's run-tab decision, and agents cost money.
- **Knowing which session belonged to which pane.** The picker handles it. Correlating #144's
  captured scrollback against candidate session files is a possible later refinement.
- **Agent detection by process inspection.** Impossible on this libghostty pin — verified, no pid,
  no pty fd.
- **A third agent backend.** `AgentBackend` is a two-case enum; adding one is additive later.
- **Persisting anything about agents.** No session id, no backend, no new `WindowSession` field.

## What already exists

| Need | Existing code | Reused? |
|---|---|---|
| Picker-form argv construction | `AgentInvocationBuilder.claudeInline` | ✅ same enum, new case |
| Executable name resolution | `AgentBackend.executable` + `/usr/bin/env` on the augmented PATH | ✅ |
| Opening an interactive agent from a click | `TerminalStatusBar` Investigate → `sessions.addRunTab` | ✅ D2b is this precedent |
| Per-tab agent state keyed on `TerminalTab.ID` | `TerminalAgentManager.banners` | ⚠️ **second dictionary**, not this one (C1) |
| Pane-lifecycle cleanup | `TerminalAgentManager.tabClosed` | ✅ extend |
| Default-off fixture path seam | `UITestFixture.sessionFilePath` | ✅ mirrored |
| Status-bar segment composition | `TerminalStatusBar` (5 segments today) | ✅ |

## Open decision for the user

**D2 is a product call, not an engineering one.** (b) is the safer build; (a) is the feature the
issue describes. Everything else in this plan is settled.

So adding `.resume` to `AgentBannerState` is wrong, and a single enum value could not represent diagnosis plus resume simultaneously.

The plan overstates this as “the biggest thing” and assumes the issue necessarily requires a sixth case. It is a routine state-model mismatch, not an architectural crisis.

Concrete fix: keep resume state independent from `AgentBannerState`, but do not automatically put a second unrelated concern on `TerminalAgentManager`; see D1 below.

### C2 — Existing banner presentation is failure-specific

**Severity: medium — real.**

Evidence:

- The status-bar control is explicitly a diagnosis popover ([TerminalStatusBar.swift:9](/Users/joelmoss/dev/workroom/macapp/WorkroomApp/Views/TerminalStatusBar.swift:9)).
- Its tooltip and accessibility label say “diagnosis” ([TerminalStatusBar.swift:256](/Users/joelmoss/dev/workroom/macapp/WorkroomApp/Views/TerminalStatusBar.swift:256)).
- Awaiting/ready/failure states are deliberately failure-red ([TerminalStatusBar.swift:251](/Users/joelmoss/dev/workroom/macapp/WorkroomApp/Views/TerminalStatusBar.swift:251), [TerminalStatusBar.swift:286](/Users/joelmoss/dev/workroom/macapp/WorkroomApp/Views/TerminalStatusBar.swift:286)).
- The tab-strip badge likewise means a live diagnosis ([TerminalTabStrip.swift:147](/Users/joelmoss/dev/workroom/macapp/WorkroomApp/Views/TerminalTabStrip.swift:147)).

Concrete fix: use a separate, direct resume affordance. Do not reuse `AgentBannerViewModel`, diagnosis tinting, tooltip, badge, or popover.

### C3 — Claude slug handling

**Severity: high — not established by repository code, and the proposed implementation remains unsafe.**

Nothing in the named code implements or documents Claude’s private storage slug. The plan’s claim comes from inspecting one machine’s private store, not from repository evidence, and it explicitly leaves `_` unresolved.

Worse, its proposed `resolvingSymlinksInPath()` before slugging changes the path string that Claude itself may have used. A session launched from `/work/link` may be stored under the textual symlink path, while the plan looks under the resolved target. Lowercasing is also wrong on case-sensitive APFS or external volumes.

Concrete fix:

- Treat the slug only as a candidate-directory optimization, not proof of identity.
- Validate candidate session metadata against the exact saved cwd where the format supports it.
- Do not lowercase paths globally.
- Define explicit symlink semantics and test both textual and resolved paths.
- Do not ship a guessed reverse-engineered transform with “accepted” collisions as the sole identity check.

### C4 — `savedAt` is discarded

**Severity: low — real, but the proposed ownership is poor.**

Evidence:

- `SessionFile` contains `savedAt` ([SessionSnapshot.swift:480](/Users/joelmoss/dev/workroom/macapp/WorkroomApp/Core/SessionSnapshot.swift:480)).
- `ProjectStore.loadSessionIfNeeded()` retains only `file.windows` ([ProjectStore.swift:209](/Users/joelmoss/dev/workroom/macapp/WorkroomApp/Core/ProjectStore.swift:209)).

Concrete fix: carry `savedAt` inside a one-shot restore context returned with claimed windows. Do not add a long-lived mutable `ProjectStore.savedAt` property that survives after restore and can accidentally be reused by later windows or reloads.

### C5 — Restored tabs are not marked

**Severity: low — factually real, proposed fix unnecessary.**

Evidence:

- `restore` creates fresh ordinary `TerminalTab` values through `makeTerminalTab` ([TerminalSessions.swift:612](/Users/joelmoss/dev/workroom/macapp/WorkroomApp/Core/TerminalSessions.swift:612)).
- `TerminalTab` has no restoration provenance ([TerminalSessions.swift:14](/Users/joelmoss/dev/workroom/macapp/WorkroomApp/Core/TerminalSessions.swift:14)).
- `restore` currently returns only an `Int`, losing the identities it just created ([TerminalSessions.swift:601](/Users/joelmoss/dev/workroom/macapp/WorkroomApp/Core/TerminalSessions.swift:601), [TerminalSessions.swift:652](/Users/joelmoss/dev/workroom/macapp/WorkroomApp/Core/TerminalSessions.swift:652)).

A persistent `wasRestored` boolean is needless state. The restore call already knows exactly which terminal tabs it created.

Concrete fix: return `[RestoredTerminal]` containing `tabID`, target ID, and effective cwd. Start discovery from that result. Newly created ⌘T tabs can never enter the discovery input, so no permanent flag is needed.

## 2. D2: `addRunTab` is wrong

**Severity: critical.**

The plan’s statement that direct `addRunTab` is “tracked by `AppStore.RunState` and `WindowRegistry.runOwner`” is false.

`addRunTab` only creates and inserts a fixed-command surface. Its own documentation says the caller owns run state and exit wiring ([TerminalSessions.swift:912](/Users/joelmoss/dev/workroom/macapp/WorkroomApp/Core/TerminalSessions.swift:912), [TerminalSessions.swift:940](/Users/joelmoss/dev/workroom/macapp/WorkroomApp/Core/TerminalSessions.swift:940)).

Actual run tracking happens only in `AppStore.startRunCommand`:

- It creates supervisor/pid-file machinery.
- It writes `runStates`.
- It wires `onChildExited`.
- It installs graceful close handling.

See [AppStore.swift:1923](/Users/joelmoss/dev/workroom/macapp/WorkroomApp/Core/AppStore.swift:1923), [AppStore.swift:1932](/Users/joelmoss/dev/workroom/macapp/WorkroomApp/Core/AppStore.swift:1932), [AppStore.swift:1950](/Users/joelmoss/dev/workroom/macapp/WorkroomApp/Core/AppStore.swift:1950), and [AppStore.swift:1958](/Users/joelmoss/dev/workroom/macapp/WorkroomApp/Core/AppStore.swift:1958).

Direct `addRunTab` therefore causes all of these failures:

- **Critical — untracked process at quit.** Quit-time detection iterates `runStates`, not surfaces ([AppStore.swift:2248](/Users/joelmoss/dev/workroom/macapp/WorkroomApp/Core/AppStore.swift:2248), [AppStore.swift:2257](/Users/joelmoss/dev/workroom/macapp/WorkroomApp/Core/AppStore.swift:2257)). The agent will be skipped by graceful teardown.
- **High — issue #7 protections are bypassed.** A raw surface close causes a PTY hangup; the code explicitly warns this can orphan descendants ([AppStore.swift:1964](/Users/joelmoss/dev/workroom/macapp/WorkroomApp/Core/AppStore.swift:1964)).
- **High — `WindowRegistry.runOwner` does nothing.** It checks another window’s `runStates` ([WindowRegistry.swift:208](/Users/joelmoss/dev/workroom/macapp/WorkroomApp/Core/WindowRegistry.swift:208)). A direct agent run is invisible, so two restored windows can launch duplicates.
- **High — trying to add it to `RunState` is also wrong.** There is one run state per target ([AppStore.swift:1310](/Users/joelmoss/dev/workroom/macapp/WorkroomApp/Core/AppStore.swift:1310)). An agent session would collide with the project’s configured dev-server run, inherit Run/Stop/Restart UI, and produce toasts whose command is read from project run configuration ([AppStore.swift:1471](/Users/joelmoss/dev/workroom/macapp/WorkroomApp/Core/AppStore.swift:1471)).
- **High — it deliberately will not restore.** Any surface with a command is excluded from session capture ([TerminalSessions.swift:211](/Users/joelmoss/dev/workroom/macapp/WorkroomApp/Core/TerminalSessions.swift:211)). The user resumes an agent, quits again, and the resumed pane disappears from the next restore.
- **Medium — wrong UX semantics.** Fixed commands use `wait_after_command` ([GhosttySurfaceView.swift:255](/Users/joelmoss/dev/workroom/macapp/WorkroomApp/Core/GhosttySurfaceView.swift:255)); after exit, the next key closes the tab ([GhosttySurfaceView.swift:989](/Users/joelmoss/dev/workroom/macapp/WorkroomApp/Core/GhosttySurfaceView.swift:989)).
- **Medium — it does not appear “beside” the restored pane.** `addRunTab` appends a solo tab and focuses it ([TerminalSessions.swift:943](/Users/joelmoss/dev/workroom/macapp/WorkroomApp/Core/TerminalSessions.swift:943)). It creates no split.
- **High — it violates the feature itself.** The requested action is in the restored pane. A new, non-restorable Run tab leaves that pane inert.

The existing Investigate handlers directly calling `addRunTab` ([TerminalStatusBar.swift:267](/Users/joelmoss/dev/workroom/macapp/WorkroomApp/Views/TerminalStatusBar.swift:267), [TerminalTabStrip.swift:437](/Users/joelmoss/dev/workroom/macapp/WorkroomApp/Views/TerminalTabStrip.swift:437)) are evidence of an existing lifecycle hole, not a precedent to duplicate.

Concrete fix: execute the static picker command in the restored login shell, but only while the pane is pristine. Track user input/paste since restore and remove the offer after the first input event. On a click, atomically consume the offer and send the fixed command plus Return. The comment at `sendText` forbids auto-running an **AI-suggested fix**, not a static command explicitly authorized by a button click ([GhosttySurfaceView.swift:970](/Users/joelmoss/dev/workroom/macapp/WorkroomApp/Core/GhosttySurfaceView.swift:970)).

If product insists on a new pane, build a separate interactive-agent lifecycle. Do not mislabel it as issue #7 Run state.

## 3. D1: second dictionary

**Severity: medium.**

Independent resume and diagnosis state is correct. A second `[tabID: ...]` dictionary on `TerminalAgentManager` is not the cleanest shape:

- The manager’s documented responsibility is failure classification and diagnosis ([TerminalAgentManager.swift:55](/Users/joelmoss/dev/workroom/macapp/WorkroomApp/Core/TerminalAgentManager.swift:55)).
- Resume discovery has different lifecycle, IO, cancellation, and cost semantics.
- Two dictionaries plus `wasRestored` create three representations that must agree.
- `[AgentBackend]` permits duplicates and gives ordering accidental semantic weight.

Concrete fix:

- Have `TerminalSessions.restore` return restored-terminal descriptors.
- Put discovery state in a small `AgentResumeCoordinator`/`ResumeOfferStore`.
- Key it by tab ID with a value such as `{ offers: Set<AgentBackend>, generation, discoveryTask }`.
- Atomically consume an offer before launching.
- Let `tabClosed` notify that coordinator alongside the diagnosis manager.

If avoiding another object is important, use one composite per-tab state rather than parallel dictionaries:

```swift
struct TabAgentState {
  var diagnosis: AgentBannerState?
  var resumeOffers: Set<AgentBackend>
}
```

But that still leaves discovery awkwardly owned by a diagnosis manager.

## 4. D3: 24 hours

**Severity: high.**

This converts “likely associated with the restored session” into “someone used an agent somewhere in this directory yesterday.”

The underlying timestamp is already weak: `savedAt` is global to the entire session document, not per pane, per cwd, or per agent. Widening it by 288× does not repair that missing identity; it multiplies false positives.

Other defects:

- A future-mtime window is not harmless. Corrupt or manipulated timestamps can keep offers alive.
- Three Codex day directories can contain thousands of rollout files.
- A 24-hour Claude match will commonly trigger for routine daily use, even if the restored pane never contained Claude.
- The picker being interactive does not make a misleading button free. It leaks session existence, starts an executable, invites billed work, and trains users to click an unreliable signal.
- Lowercasing paths because the “default APFS volume” is insensitive is invalid for case-sensitive and external volumes.
- Symlink resolution can intentionally merge two textual workrooms into one identity.

Concrete fix: keep the issue’s conservative five-minute window initially, preferably one-sided with a small clock-skew allowance. Better still, correlate with restored scrollback or persist non-sensitive agent provenance prospectively. Do not pretend a 24-hour directory-level heuristic identifies a pane.

## 5. Entirely missed

### Unbounded discovery IO

**Severity: critical.**

“One background unit” is not a bound. Synchronous directory enumeration inside a detached task is not cooperatively cancellable. With thousands of rollouts, it can run long after every relevant pane closes.

Concrete fix: index each Codex file once per launch, deduplicate cwds, use bounded reads through `FileHandle`, impose maximum files/bytes/wall time, check cancellation between entries, and publish partial/no result on deadline.

### Restore watchdog interaction

**Severity: high.**

`restorePersistedSessionIfPending` calls `finishSessionRestore` in a `defer` ([AppStore+Session.swift:159](/Users/joelmoss/dev/workroom/macapp/WorkroomApp/Core/AppStore+Session.swift:159)). The watchdog fires after 15 seconds and freezes session writes if any window remains incomplete ([ProjectStore.swift:179](/Users/joelmoss/dev/workroom/macapp/WorkroomApp/Core/ProjectStore.swift:179), [ProjectStore.swift:223](/Users/joelmoss/dev/workroom/macapp/WorkroomApp/Core/ProjectStore.swift:223)).

If discovery is awaited before the defer, a large store can freeze persistence. If it is fire-and-forget, each window starts its own “single batch” while sibling windows are still restoring. The plan has no global completion point or ownership.

Concrete fix: finish structural restore first. Then schedule discovery asynchronously from returned descriptors. Use a process-wide discovery index/cache shared by windows.

### Two windows restoring the same workroom

**Severity: high.**

Fresh tab IDs are deliberately global across windows ([TerminalSessions.swift:588](/Users/joelmoss/dev/workroom/macapp/WorkroomApp/Core/TerminalSessions.swift:588)), but cwd matching will give both windows identical offers. Direct `addRunTab` bypasses `runOwner`, allowing duplicate agents and duplicate billed sessions.

Concrete fix: consume atomically per tab, suppress double-clicks, and introduce explicit interactive-agent ownership if cross-window duplication is disallowed. Add a two-window restore test.

### Symlink and path-boundary security

**Severity: high.**

The plan follows symlinks and case-folds without defining trust boundaries. Candidate session files themselves may be symlinks. A malicious project-local action could arrange links causing Workroom to inspect unrelated files under the user account.

Concrete fix: require regular files, reject symlinked candidate files/directories unless explicitly supported, enforce containment under the configured agent root, avoid global lowercasing, and test case-sensitive volumes and symlinked workrooms.

### Scrollback replay ordering

**Severity: medium.**

Issue #144 intentionally defers sidecar IO until a pane mounts ([GhosttySurfaceView.swift:156](/Users/joelmoss/dev/workroom/macapp/WorkroomApp/Core/GhosttySurfaceView.swift:156)); replay then occurs synchronously during surface creation ([GhosttySurfaceView.swift:290](/Users/joelmoss/dev/workroom/macapp/WorkroomApp/Core/GhosttySurfaceView.swift:290)). The plan adds eager, unrelated store scanning for every restored pane, including panes whose scrollback may never be loaded.

Concrete fix: do not claim this preserves scrollback “beside” anything. Test that discovery cannot delay surface creation/replay and that clicking resume consumes the offer without altering restored history.

### Repeated paid execution

**Severity: high.**

The offer is never removed on click in the design. A double-click or repeated clicks can spawn multiple CLIs. The T1 “spike” itself runs `claude -p 'hi'`, which can incur cost and mutate the developer’s real Claude history.

Concrete fix: delete T1. Use checked-in fixtures or a documented compatibility table. Consume/disable the offer before execution and require a new explicit action to retry after a failed picker launch.

### Invocation abstraction is dishonest

**Severity: medium.**

The plan claims argv is “built as data,” but `addRunTab` accepts a single command string ([TerminalSessions.swift:940](/Users/joelmoss/dev/workroom/macapp/WorkroomApp/Core/TerminalSessions.swift:940)), which is assigned to Ghostty’s command field ([GhosttySurfaceView.swift:258](/Users/joelmoss/dev/workroom/macapp/WorkroomApp/Core/GhosttySurfaceView.swift:258)). The proposed `AgentInvocation` must therefore be serialized back into a command line somewhere the plan does not specify or test.

Concrete fix: for the two static picker commands, use audited constants. If arbitrary argv is ever needed, add a single tested shell-command encoder or a spawn API that accepts argv.

### Error handling is inadequate

**Severity: medium.**

“No history,” unreadable root, permission denied, malformed files, scan deadline, unsupported schema, CLI missing, and CLI spawn failure all collapse to silence or a shell error. The plan’s “critical gaps: 0” claim is false.

Concrete fix: keep expected absence silent, log bounded discovery failures without paths/session contents, and show a transient user-facing error when an explicit click cannot start the CLI.

### Test plan misses the action

**Severity: critical.**

The UI tests only assert button visibility and that launch does not spawn a process. They never click the button.

Required additions:

- Exactly one click starts exactly one picker command.
- Double-click/repeated click cannot start duplicates.
- Offer disappears atomically on action and tab closure.
- Existing typed input suppresses the offer or prevents execution.
- Two-window same-workroom restore.
- Existing configured Run command remains unaffected.
- Quit/window-close teardown with an active resumed agent.
- Resume pane remains persistable on the next launch.
- Symlinked cwd, case-sensitive paths, and slug collisions.
- Thousands of rollout files, deadline, cancellation, and bounded memory.
- Restore watchdog plus slow discovery.
- Scrollback replay ordering.
- Missing executable and failed spawn.
- No live agent process in tests; all execution must use an injected fake.

## 6. What should be cut

Cut these outright:

- **D2/addRunTab.** It is the wrong lifecycle and violates the feature.
- **The 24-hour window and symmetric future matching.**
- **T1’s real `claude -p` probe.** Tests must not spend money or mutate private agent state.
- **`TerminalTab.wasRestored`.** Return restored IDs instead.
- **Unconditional path lowercasing.**
- **The claim that slug collisions are “accepted” without metadata validation.**
- **The single unbounded detached batch.**
- **The grep gate for `--continue`/`--last`.** A repository-wide text ban is brittle and unrelated to runtime correctness; test the invocation builder/action instead.
- **The “critical gaps: 0” assertion.** It is demonstrably false.

The plan needs redesign around executing a one-shot, user-authorized static command in a pristine restored shell, with bounded discovery and explicit lifecycle ownership.
